title: The Bakery: Sharing & Halving
strapline: Cut the cake so it's fair — the oldest maths problem there is.
intent: Children meet fair sharing and halving through the powerful, real motive of 'that's not fair, mine's smaller'.
Children divide quantities — biscuits between plates, a cake into equal parts — and check that shares are equal.
Children explore doubling and halving practically: two of everything for two customers, half each for two friends.
Children count with purpose — how many buns are needed, how many are left — in a busy, sociable role-play.
Children develop the language of fairness and fractions in plain words: half, whole, each, the same, equal, share.
implementation: Set up a bakery with playdough, cutters, a rolling pin, trays, and 'customers' (children or teddies) to serve.
Pose real sharing problems: 'four buns and two customers — how many each so it's fair?'
Model halving out loud, cutting a dough cake: 'half for you, half for me — are they the same size?'
Introduce 'each' and 'equal' as the fairness test — count each plate and compare, redistributing until it's fair.
Add an ordering pad so children write down how many of each item a customer wants, then bake exactly that many.
Let real cooking sessions carry the same maths — dividing dough, sharing out ingredients, counting cases.
Play the fussy customer sometimes: 'mine looks smaller!' so children have to make the shares truly equal.
key_questions: How can we share these fairly so everyone gets the same?
If we cut it in half, how many pieces will there be?
How many buns does each customer get?
Are these two halves really the same size — how can we tell?
We have six and there are three of us — how many each?

impact.text: Children share a quantity equally between people or plates.
Children halve an object into two equal parts and check they match.
Children count with purpose to bake and serve the right number.
Children use fairness and fraction words — half, whole, each, equal, share.
Children negotiate, take turns and resolve 'that's not fair' together.
Children persist to make shares genuinely equal.

enhancements: Playdough, cutters and a set of matching plates for the sharing.
A real baking session — dividing dough into equal rolls, halving apples.
An order pad and a chalkboard price list to add counting and money.
Pizza-slice props for exploring halves and quarters of a circle.
A doubling challenge: the birthday order is 'twice as many, please'.
A tea-party small world with cups and cakes to share among teddies.

playing_exploring: Children run the bakery, choosing what to bake and who to serve.
The role-play makes sharing and halving something they want to get right.
active_learning: Children keep adjusting the shares until everyone agrees it's fair.
The pride of a fair share drives them to check and re-check.
creating_thinking: Children work out a way to share and test whether it's equal.
They plan an order, count what's needed and solve the shortfall.
